transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-18
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (CSM), Lena Ko (SE), Maya Chen (OpalCare - Head of ML), Daniel Ruiz (OpalCare - VP Eng), Priya Nair (OpalCare - DevOps), Samir Patel (OpalCare - Security)

Summary (auto): Kickoff for onboarding; high level goals, timeline, security checklist, initial infra assumptions, next steps and owners.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Sofia from Redwood, I'll kick us off. We also have Arjun and Lena from our CS and SE teams. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Maya: Good, thanks. Excited to get started.
[00:15] Daniel: Yep, thanks. We're hoping to get the pilot running within the next 4 weeks.
[00:25] Sofia: Great. High level agenda - confirm goals, where you're running today, security and compliance needs, pick a deployment mode (hosted, dedicated or private), and assign next steps.
[00:35] Arjun: Quick intro from our side - I'll be the primary contact for onboarding logistics and success criteria. Lena will handle infra and performance.
[00:45] Lena: Hi all. I'll want to dig into your traffic patterns, peak qps, typical sequence lengths so we can size the pilot appropriately.
[00:55] Maya: For context, our current stack is a mixture of in-house models and OpenAI usage for chat and summarization. We have strict PHI handling rules in some flows and want to avoid any data residency issues.
[01:10] Priya: On infra, we're on AWS, us-west-2 primarily. We use KMS for key management and have strict egress and VPC peering policies. We'll likely want VPC peering or Private deployment for production.
[01:30] Samir: From security, we need SOC2 level controls, audit logs, support for our KMS, and SSO/SAML. Also encryption at rest and in transit.
[01:45] Sofia: Totally expected. We support SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning, Redwood Private for on-prem/VPC and Dedicated for reserved pools. We'll share our SOC2 and security deck after this call.
[02:05] Daniel: Can you clarify Dedicated vs Hosted - costs and latency trade-offs?
[02:20] Lena: Sure. Hosted is fastest to start but has more noisy neighbor risk; Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs and predictable latency, and Private gives you the most isolation but higher ops. Lena: For throughput, we can estimate batching and KV caching benefits.
[02:45] Maya: We're worried about cost - we have heavy summarization workloads and want to keep token costs down.
[02:55] Sofia: We'll propose optimized quantization profiles and batching configs; Redwood Optimize can suggest batching and quantization. Also we'll provide sample TCO comparisons for hosted vs dedicated.
[03:15] Priya: On networking - do you support VPC peering or do we need to open egress?
[03:25] Lena: We support both. For Private deployment we run in your VPC. For Dedicated we can do VPC peering or PrivateLink; we'll need to see your network diagram.
[03:40] Samir: And KMS? Can you integrate with our AWS KMS/HSM?
[03:46] Sofia: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS for Private and Dedicated deployments; for hosted we offer managed keys but can discuss bring-your-own-key options.
[04:00] [Speaker 2]: There's also the question of audit logs retention - how long do you keep traces?
[04:10] Arjun: By default we retain operational logs for 90 days; extended retention is an add on. We'll share exact SLAs and retention options in the security pack.
[04:25] Daniel: Pilot success criteria - we'd measure latency under 95th percentile, cost per 1k tokens, and regression on output quality vs our current baseline.
[04:40] Arjun: Proposed pilot: 2-week run, synthetic load up to 2k qps for brief spikes, production-like prompts for quality evals, and ramp to steady 200-400 qps.
[04:55] Maya: That sounds reasonable. We also want to include a prompt set for evals and automatic regression alerts.
[05:05] Lena: We'll set up a small canary model and use continuous evals. For the throughput estimate I need sequence length distribution and tokenization examples.
[05:25] Priya: I'll share a sample dataset and our typical sequence histogram.
[05:30] [00:05:30] Sofia: Great, Priya - please add that to the drive link we'll send.
[05:35] [00:05:35] Daniel: On the timeline, if we start now, can we be in pilot by June 29?
[05:45] Sofia: We can aim for that if we get network diagrams and SSO set up within this week. Arjun: I'll follow up with the success criteria doc by Friday.
[06:00] Lena: Action items for me: run an initial sizing for Dedicated vs Hosted for your traffic and produce expected latency and cost numbers.
[06:10] Maya: One question - do you support prefix/KV cache to reduce token usage for chat flows?
[06:20] Lena: Yes, Redwood has prefix and KV caching; that tends to help conversational workloads a lot. We'll include caching recommendations.
[06:30] Samir: Any compliance certifications we should be aware of beyond SOC2?
[06:36] Sofia: We have SOC2 in process; we also support audit logs, RBAC, and can discuss HIPAA contracts for PHI. We'll share legal docs.
[06:50] [00:06:50] Priya: For SSO - we use Okta. Is there a SCIM integration?
[06:56] Arjun: Yes, SCIM is supported for user provisioning. We'll send the Okta config guide.
[07:05] [00:07:05] Daniel: Something else - do you have any benchmarking notes with OpenAI or Anthropic? We've seen varied latencies across vendors.
[07:18] Lena: We have internal benchmarks; we'll share a short spreadsheet showing p95 latencies on typical seq lengths and the tradeoffs across models. Note sometimes the model names in our docs get mangled - you might see Redwood Dedi or Redwood Dedicate in early notes, apologies.
[07:35] Maya: That's okay. We're mainly interested in stability and predictable cost.
[07:40] Sofia: Recap of action items and owners - Arjun will send pilot success criteria and schedule the architecture deep dive with Lena, Lena will produce throughput estimates and caching recommendations, Priya will share KMS and VPC diagrams, Sofia will send security pack and contract draft.
[07:58] Arjun: We'll also set up a shared drive with the prompt set for evals.
[08:05] [00:08:05] Priya: One technical detail - do you support truncation or streaming for long responses? We have some flows that stream long summaries.
[08:15] Lena: We support streaming responses and have rate limits; we'll configure the route for your streaming flows.
[08:25] Sofia: Next meeting - architecture deep dive targeted for one week from today. I'll send a calendar invite.
[08:35] Daniel: Great. Anything else from you, Maya?
[08:40] Maya: No, thank you. Looking forward to the docs and the pilot.
[08:45] Sofia: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs. Bye.

End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription had a few mis-attributions and "Redwood Dedicated" was sometimes transcribed as "Redwood Dedi" or "Redwood Dedicate". Some timestamps approximate.
file_notes: Recorded via Zoom, Fireflies automatic transcript. Contains customer-sensitive items like KMS and pilot targets; treat as internal-only until customer approves sharing externally.
